candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is a 76-year-old male American, White and non-Hispanic, living in Colorado. He is married to Elise; they have no children. Their gross household income is above $200,000, from his retirement income and occasional engineering consulting, Elise’s pension, and investment distributions. Philip identifies as moderately conservative: he values tradition, personal responsibility, and limits on government, while accepting public programs such as Medicare and Social Security. He enjoys reading for pleasure, especially biographies, engineering histories, and books about boats.
candidates.life_course: He spent most of his career as a structural engineer, eventually leading a small consulting practice. The practical problem-solving of the work suited him, and he kept an interest in woodworking that began with repairs around his first home. He and Elise have been married for decades; she likes being on the water but leaves the fine sanding and measurements to him.
candidates.daily_life: Philip now divides his week between occasional engineering reviews and restoring a small wooden boat in a well-equipped workshop. Elise sometimes helps keep his notes and joins him for short outings on the water. He likes projects with visible progress, and he reads a chapter or two most evenings, often marking passages he wants to bring up later.
candidates.travel: He travels to encounter working waterfronts, see how older boats are built and maintained, and get time aboard a vessel rather than merely look at one. A past trip to coastal Maine, where he watched a restorer explain a repair and then sailed with Elise, convinced him that these trips are worth planning around craft as well as scenery. They usually travel together, driving for nearer destinations and flying farther afield; he prefers a comfortable inn, a few planned visits to boatyards or maritime collections, and unhurried days near the water. He brings a notebook and is happy to spend an afternoon talking shop.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is direct, exacting, and more animated when discussing how something is made than when discussing himself. He can sound like he is correcting people even when he means to be helpful. With friends, he enjoys a dry joke and will happily draw out a story about a stubborn repair.

candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is an 81-year-old male American, White and non-Hispanic, who lives in Montana. He is married to Beatrice, and they have no children. Their gross household income exceeds $200,000, supported by investments and retirement income following the sale of his food-service supply business, along with Beatrice’s retirement income. He is moderately conservative, placing importance on tradition, personal responsibility, and limited government, while accepting useful public programs. He reads for leisure, particularly food memoirs, novels, and cookbooks that explain the people and history behind a dish.
candidates.life_course: Philip learned early to cook for a crowd and later spent his working life supplying restaurants and institutional kitchens. He enjoyed the relationships with cooks as much as the business side, and after selling the company he began spending more time experimenting at home. Beatrice is an enthusiastic co-taster and a steadier planner than he is.
candidates.daily_life: Most weeks include a trip to a market, a new recipe, or a meal shared with friends. Philip enjoys making dinner collaboratively with Beatrice, then asking guests what they noticed in the food. He keeps handwritten notes about adjustments and reads cookbooks as stories, not just instruction manuals. His kitchen can get cluttered when he has several ideas going at once.
candidates.travel: He wants trips to reveal how a region’s food connects to its landscape, local habits, and family traditions; an excellent meal matters, but so does learning how it came to be. On a past visit to southern Louisiana, he spent time at markets, tried unfamiliar dishes, and came home practicing a preparation he had watched a local cook make. He and Beatrice often choose a small inn or rental with a kitchen, rent a car outside a city, and leave room for spontaneous stops. A market visit or cooking lesson may anchor a day, but he also likes long meals and conversation with the people they meet.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is sociable and quick to invite people into a plan, sometimes before Beatrice has agreed to host. He has strong opinions about seasoning and will defend them cheerfully. He remembers who told him a story or shared a recipe and likes to retell both, with generous embellishment.

candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is a 79-year-old male American, White and non-Hispanic, living in Colorado. He is married to Anne, and they have no children. Their gross household income is at least $200,000, from the proceeds and investments of his former land-surveying firm, along with retirement income. Philip is moderately conservative, emphasizing personal responsibility, tradition, and limits on government while accepting public programs including Medicare. He reads for pleasure, especially natural history, geology, and a few well-worn novels.
candidates.life_course: He built a successful surveying business and spent decades outdoors measuring land, which taught him to notice slopes, water, and weather. Retirement did not make him want a packed calendar; it gave him more time to fish. Anne is happy to join some trips for walks and scenery, while understanding that a fishing day often includes long stretches when he has little to say.
candidates.daily_life: Philip spends free time fly-fishing, usually alone or with one longtime friend, and keeps brief notes about water conditions and what he observed. He enjoys the concentration more than the catch. At home he reads, maintains his equipment, and takes ordinary walks with Anne. He dislikes turning every interest into a club or a competition.
candidates.travel: The purpose of a fishing trip is to spend sustained time reading a river and its surroundings: the changing light, the current, and the life along the banks matter as much as whether fish are biting. On a past weeklong trip to an Idaho river with his friend, they fished some mornings and spent others looking at the canyon and talking about its geology; Philip still recalls a quiet, foggy morning more vividly than his best catch. He generally drives with his gear, stays in a cabin or modest lodge, and plans around a few days at one stretch of water rather than racing between stops. Anne sometimes comes along and makes her own plans for part of the day.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is laconic and wry, and he does not rush to fill silences. He can be impatient with crowds and with people who treat the outdoors as a backdrop for constant noise. Among trusted companions, a small observation or deadpan remark is his way of showing affection.

candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is an 84-year-old male American, White and non-Hispanic, residing in Idaho. He is married to Margaret; they have no children. Their gross household income is over $200,000, coming from retirement income, investments, and the long-term proceeds of his career as a commercial attorney, as well as Margaret’s retirement income. He describes himself as moderately conservative, valuing tradition, personal responsibility, and restrained government while supporting public programs he considers useful. He enjoys reading for leisure, especially music biographies, history, and literary fiction.
candidates.life_course: Philip sang bass in choirs from early adulthood and kept singing after retiring from law. He likes the discipline of rehearsals and the shared work of bringing separate voices into one sound. Margaret enjoys concerts and travels with him, though she does not want every conversation at home to become a debate about tempo or phrasing.
candidates.daily_life: His free time centers on choir rehearsals, listening to recordings, and reading about composers and performers. He is active in the social life around the chorus, organizing informal dinners and trading opinions after practice. At home, he sometimes sings a passage to explain what he means, whether or not anyone asked for a demonstration.
candidates.travel: Philip travels to hear live choral and classical music in places where the performance itself feels different from listening at home. He is fascinated by how a hall or church carries a bass line and how a familiar piece changes under another conductor. On a past trip to Vienna with Margaret, hearing a choral work in a resonant church made him pay closer attention to the relationship between architecture and sound. They typically fly for long trips, stay near the venues, and plan around a small number of performances rather than filling every day. He likes having time afterward to walk, read the program, and argue amiably about what they heard.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is theatrical, warm, and prone to interrupt when he is excited. He tells stories with a flourish and enjoys spirited disagreement, especially about music, but remembers to ask others what they heard. He is less patient with people who dismiss an unfamiliar piece without listening.
